# Fixed signatures over the 28-byte ASCII message "weaver-dnssec backend parity", made once with
# local tools so every run checks the same bytes, and neither backend made them.
# openssl-p256, openssl-p384: OpenSSL 4.1.0. openssl genpkey -algorithm EC -pkeyopt
#   ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 (P-384); key = x || y from openssl pkey -pubout -outform DER; openssl
#   dgst -sha256 (-sha384) -sign, DER r and s rewritten as fixed-width r || s.
# openssl-ml-dsa-44: OpenSSL 4.1.0. openssl genpkey -algorithm ML-DSA-44; key = the last 1312
#   bytes of openssl pkey -pubout -outform DER; openssl pkeyutl -sign -rawin (empty context).
# python-ed25519-torsion-*: Python 3.15 affine Edwards arithmetic. a = SHA-512("weaver-dnssec
#   parity torsion key") mod L; the key is aB + T, T of order 8 (the torsion part, [L]Q, of the
#   first decodable y >= 2 whose [4][L]Q is not the identity). Nonce r = SHA-512("weaver-dnssec
#   parity nonce" || i, 4-byte big-endian) mod L for i = 0, 1, ...; k = SHA-512(R || key || M)
#   mod L; s = r + k a mod L. The cofactorless check holds only when k is a multiple of 8; the
#   cofactored check holds for both. Each line is the first i with that property.
# Columns: label, DNSSEC algorithm, public key (hex), signature (hex), expected result.
